entities.summary:
Thutmose, a master sculptor of the Amarna style, flourished around 1350 BC, and is thought to have been the official court sculptor of the Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten in the latter part of his reign. The discovery of a ruined house and studio complex in Akhetaten, known today as Amarna, in early December 1912, provided valuable insights into his life and work.

Thutmose's significance lies in his contributions to Ancient Egyptian art, particularly in the Amarna style, which revolutionized sculpture and architecture in the region. His works, often featuring naturalistic depictions of humans and animals, have had a lasting impact on the development of Egyptian art.

The legacy of Thutmose can be seen in the many artists and sculptors who followed in his footsteps, including the famous sculptor, Senemut, who is believed to have been his apprentice.

A striking statistic illustrating the impact of Thutmose's work is the number of his works that have been discovered in the Amarna ruins, with over 100 sculptures and reliefs attributed to him.
